paragraphs: On Saturday afternoon, Ben came to town on his blue scooter, and Tom walked beside him. They stopped at a store near the market to buy a notebook. Ben left his scooter next to the wall by the door. Ten minutes later, the boys came out of the store. The wall was empty.

"Hey!" said Ben. "My scooter is not here." "Are you sure that you left it here?" asked Tom. "Yes, it was next to this wall," said Ben. "Somebody took it, and it is lost." "Let's not shout," said Tom. "Let's ask the police, because the police station is beside the bus stop."

At the small police station, a police officer sat at a desk with a computer. "Good afternoon," he said. "How can I help you?" "My scooter is lost," said Ben in a small voice. "Certainly, we can help," said the police officer. "Please describe it." "It is blue, and it has a white star on the front," said Ben. "My name is on the back."

The police officer wrote everything in a notebook. "Where did you leave it, and when?" he asked. "We went into the store at about three o'clock," said Tom. "The scooter was next to the wall by the door." "Which store is it?" asked the officer. "It is the store with the green sign next to the market," said Ben. The officer took the phone and called the store.

He listened for a minute and then smiled. "Good news," he said. "The man in the store says that a customer's car was at the door." "He moved your scooter to the back of the store, because it was in the way." "He wanted to tell you, but you left the store very fast." "So it was a mistake, and nobody took it!" said Ben. "Yes, you can return to the store and get it," said the officer.

The boys walked back to the store. The man brought the blue scooter out of the back door. "I am sorry," he said. "I called you, but you did not hear me." "Thank you for keeping it safe," said Ben. "Next time, I will tell the man in the store," he said to Tom. Tom laughed and said, "And next time, please do not shout."
